architecture_principles: the unit of decision is an experiment, not a formulation
value of information is computed by a deterministic scientific tool, not by an additional language model
every registered hypothesis carries an explicit pre-result prediction rule and an explicit falsification condition
a measurement that cannot separate any registered hypothesis scores zero discrimination, and that is a scientific result rather than a defect
weight sensitivity is reported as decision stability, never as model confidence
ties in the deterministic layer are reported as ties; the tool must not manufacture a preference it does not have
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
the mechanism question and the Agent framework are separate contributions and are reported separately

candidate_space.rationale: V4 deliberately reuses the byte-identical V3 lattice. Continuous-space optimization and any new wet-lab work are out of scope, so that the measured change between V3 and V4 is the decision object and the VOI layer, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer (including the deterministic VOI tool) -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V4.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime. Its adjudication tests whether a registered hypothesis survives contact with the completed measurement. It is not a contemporaneous pre-experimental record and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_VOI_GUIDED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V4
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
turning the study into a pure AI benchmark
weakening or replacing the rheological mechanism result
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that selects the next formulation x measurement EXPERIMENT by transparent value of information, rather than selecting a formulation candidate alone.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question that the next experiment must answer, then request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations

execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, and the deterministic VOI tool that scores every formulation x measurement experiment card
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value, stating the hypotheses it separates and what each possible outcome would establish
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability of the primary observable, and whether the stated falsification criterion can actually be met by the measurement
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported VOI weight sensitivity and the skeptic's strongest objection
commit to one experiment card, or abstain, and state the acceptance and falsification criteria that will adjudicate it
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card with timestamps, model identifiers and cryptographic hashes of every input

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V4 is an independent architecture. configs/agent_v3.json, prompts/agent_v3_*.txt, src/pur_new/agent_v3.py and every frozen V3 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V4.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk

voi_tool.not_a_posterior: The local design contains six audited realizations and two thermal-hold trajectories. That does not support a calibrated Bayesian expected-information computation, so no posterior probability is fabricated. Weight sensitivity is reported instead.

planner.failure_mode: Composition-dependent viscosity growth during prolonged melt residence at 120 °C, creating unresolved thermal-hold instability.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal-hold run increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min at 120 °C, compared with 9.51% for E1 over the same measured window.
planner.least_resolved_justification: Temperature response is measured from 80 to 130 °C for several original formulations, and realized viscosity-level uncertainty is directly evidenced by three E2 runs with 2.80–3.57 max/min ratios. In contrast, the 120 °C time coordinate has only one four-point run each for E1 and E5, with no measured E2-anchor trajectory, no independent repeats, and no resin-axis comparison. The available holds also differ sharply: 9.51% versus 51.54% drift from 15 to 60 min.
measurement_requirements: Measure viscosity during a 120 °C isothermal hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min and report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 in percent without extrapolating beyond the measured window.
Use at least two independent preparations per tested composition and fully record process history so realization-state variation is not mistaken for formulation-dependent drift.
Before observing results, calculate the H-CORE prediction as 9.51% multiplied by the candidate reactive mass fraction phi_r and freeze the 2 percentage-point discrimination resolution.
Classify drift relative to the registered predictions: agreement with the linear-dilution value tests H-CORE, while drift below half that value tests H-RESIN.

To adjudicate H-DUAL, include an acrylic-only experiment and a compositionally controlled experiment with nonzero minor tackifier; an acrylic-only result in the low-drift regime would falsify the claim that tackifier is required.
Measure a fresh-sample viscosity anchor at 110 °C and verify 120 and 130 °C values where feasible, so hold drift can be interpreted separately from displacement of the realized viscosity level.
Preserve the source viscosity unit as unknown unless source-level evidence resolves it.
planner.scientific_question: For a resin-modified formulation built from the E2 reactive-core anchor, is the 120 °C matched-window drift consistent with reactive-core mass dilution alone, substantially below the linear-dilution prediction because of resin-mediated suppression, or—when acrylic-only and minor-tackifier-containing designs are contrasted—is low drift contingent on a nonzero minor-tackifier fraction?

hypotheses_not_separated: H-CORE versus H-DUAL cannot be separated if drift remains near the linear-dilution prediction, because both predict near-linear drift for an acrylic-only composition; positive establishment of H-DUAL requires a matched nonzero-tackifier experiment.

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: For reactive mass fraction 0.80, the frozen H-CORE prediction is 9.51% × 0.80 = 7.608%. If SI_15_60 is below half that value, 3.804%, the result supports H-RESIN superlinear suppression, falsifies H-CORE beyond the 2 percentage-point resolution, and directly falsifies H-DUAL because low drift was achieved with no minor tackifier.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: If SI_15_60 is at or above 7.608%, H-RESIN is falsified. A value within 2 percentage points of 7.608% supports H-CORE and is also consistent with the acrylic-only prediction of H-DUAL, but does not distinguish those two hypotheses. A value more than 2 percentage points above 7.608% would falsify the simple H-CORE scaling as well and indicate an unregistered drift-enhancing effect.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.804% to below 7.608% indicates partial suppression that meets neither the strict H-RESIN support criterion nor its falsification criterion. Values below 5.608% falsify H-CORE beyond measurement resolution without reaching the registered H-RESIN acceptance threshold; values from 5.608% to below 7.608% remain resolution-compatible with H-CORE. Follow-up with a matched nonzero-tackifier composition would still be required to establish H-DUAL positively.

proposer.primary_observable: Directly measured SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, during a 120 C hold with measurements at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min on at least two independent preparations.

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: The 15% acrylic-only hold has the same useful hypothesis geometry and lower modifier burden, but 15% is supported only as a directional lower-region point with an unverified literature fraction denominator, whereas 20% is a directly commensurate external anchor.

The 15% acrylic plus 5% tackifier composition lies inside both supported regions and directly tests H-CORE versus H-RESIN, but a low result cannot show whether acrylic alone would suffice and therefore cannot execute H-DUAL's explicit acrylic-only falsification test.

The 5% tackifier-only composition is in the repeatedly documented minor-resin cluster and can test linear dilution versus suppression, but low drift would only be consistent with H-DUAL and would not establish tackifier necessity without an acrylic-only comparator.

The anchor experiment measures reconstruction error conditional on a transferred thermal-response model rather than directly measuring the unresolved 120 C time-dependent drift, and its decision relevance is lower.

proposer.reasoning: S1C49 combines a directly supported 20% acrylic intervention with the direct, matched-window measurement of the declared failure mode. Its 7.608% linear prediction and 3.804% superlinear-suppression threshold differ by more than the frozen 2 percentage-point resolution. Unlike a tackifier-containing card, the acrylic-only design also exposes H-DUAL to its registered decisive falsification outcome: low drift without tackifier. The experiment should use at least two independently prepared samples with recorded process histories so the large known E2 realization spread is not mistaken for formulation-dependent drift.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Replace the initial S1C49 acrylic-only hold with the E2 reactive-core-only 120 C hold represented by S1C01::M-HOLD-120. This directly addresses the missing matched E2 baseline on which the proposed H-CORE benchmark depends. After that baseline is established, S1C49 and a matched nonzero-tackifier candidate should be tested under the same protocol to address H-RESIN and H-DUAL.
robustness_adjudication.departure_from_deterministic_ranking: Indeterminate rather than a demonstrated departure: the deterministic rule layer, VOI scores, ranking, and tied_top_experiment_ids were withheld, so membership of S1C49::M-HOLD-120 in the deterministic top set cannot be established from the supplied payload.
residual_decision_risk: The inventory contains multiple apparently identical reactive-core-only cards, S1C01 through S1C09, without supplied distinctions; S1C01 is selected as the first listed representative.
At least two repeats are specified, but the composition-level aggregation rule and treatment of repeats crossing decision boundaries remain unspecified.
The declared 2 percentage-point discrimination threshold lacks validation from repeated original hold measurements.
E2 shows large realization-to-realization viscosity-scale variation, so controlled and recorded process history is necessary to avoid confounding hold drift with preparation state.
Modifier reactive-group contents and effective NCO:OH remain unverified, limiting later interpretation of reactive mass fraction and chemical inertness.
An E2 baseline alone does not separate ordinary dilution from acrylic-specific suppression; an inert-dilution control would still be needed for stronger attribution.
H-DUAL cannot be positively established without matched acrylic-only and nonzero-tackifier hold experiments.
M-HOLD-120 can establish phenomenological drift differences but cannot identify the molecular encounter-frequency explanation stated within H-RESIN.
Decision-stability quantities were withheld, so robustness to VOI re-weighting remains unknown.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection undermines the central comparison rather than merely narrowing interpretation: S1C49 uses the E2 reactive core, but its 7.608% H-CORE benchmark is transferred from one unreplicated E1 hold with different NCO:OH rather than measured on E2. The first experiment should therefore be an E2 reactive-core-only matched-window 120 C hold. This establishes the relevant baseline before testing S1C49 for dilution versus superlinear suppression. It does not by itself resolve H-DUAL; that hypothesis still requires a matched acrylic-only and nonzero-tackifier contrast.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: Not assessable. The payload supplies no top_experiment_set_stability, base_margin_to_first_strictly_lower, recommendation_flip_boundary, weight terms, or perturbation results. Therefore no decision-changing scaling or scientific defensibility judgment about such a scaling can be identified.

skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: M-HOLD-120 directly measures SI_15_60, so values below 3.804% or at or above 7.608% can occur and satisfy the stated numerical criteria. Attainability does not ensure valid interpretation: replicate aggregation is unspecified, the 2 percentage-point resolution lacks repeated hold validation in the supplied data, and the H-CORE threshold relies on transferring E1 drift to the E2 core.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A non-low acrylic-only result could be presented as evidence for tackifier necessity even though no tackifier-containing comparator was measured.
objections.objection: The field hypotheses_separated lists H-DUAL, but S1C49::M-HOLD-120 contains only the 20% acrylic, 0% tackifier composition. It can falsify H-DUAL if acrylic-only drift enters a prespecified low-drift regime, but it cannot positively establish that low drift is contingent on tackifier. The proposer acknowledges this in hypotheses_not_separated and in if_intermediate, where a matched nonzero-tackifier experiment is required. Thus H-DUAL is only outcome-conditionally falsifiable, not generally separated by this experiment.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Departure from 7.608% cannot uniquely falsify reactive-core dilution scaling; it may instead reflect invalid transfer of E1's drift coefficient to the E2 core.
objections.objection: The frozen H-CORE value of 7.608% is obtained from the single E1 hold result, 9.51%, multiplied by phi_r = 0.80, although S1C49 is built from the E2 core. E1 has NCO:OH = 1.7, whereas E2 has NCO:OH = 1.8, and the payload explicitly states that no E2-anchor hold trajectory exists. Therefore the experiment compares S1C49 with an unreplicated coefficient from a different reactive-core stoichiometry rather than with a measured E2-core baseline.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low SI_15_60 could support a phenomenological improvement but could not be attributed specifically to resin-mediated superlinear suppression rather than altered stoichiometry, ordinary dilution, or realization state.
objections.objection: S1C49 simultaneously adds 20% acrylic-like modifier and reduces the reactive mass fraction from 1.00 to 0.80. There is no E2 hold control, no chemically inert 20% dilution control, and no verification in the proposed protocol that the acrylic contributes no NCO-reactive groups. The supplied stoichiometry note specifically requires recalculation if a modifier contributes reactive OH or another NCO-reactive group. Consequently mass dilution, altered effective stoichiometry, acrylic-specific interactions, and preparation-state changes remain confounded.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The primary measurement remains direct, but hypothesis classification can become post hoc when independent repeats disagree.
objections.objection: The per-run observable SI_15_60 is directly calculated from measured eta_15 and eta_60 and requires no fit, extrapolation, or imputation, so that part survives scrutiny. However, the protocol requires at least two independent preparations without specifying whether the adjudicated composition-level value is the mean, median, each repeat separately, or a confidence-bound estimate. No rule is supplied for repeats that fall on opposite sides of 3.804%, 5.608%, or 7.608%.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: The experiment can generate nominally falsifying numbers, but borderline or discordant results may not produce a reproducible falsification decision.
objections.objection: The numerical criteria are physically attainable because M-HOLD-120 can directly return values below 3.804% or at or above 7.608%. Nevertheless, practical adjudication is incomplete: the frozen 2 percentage-point resolution is not supported by repeated E1, E2, or E5 hold measurements in the payload, and the protocol does not define how that resolution applies to the required replicate results. The interval from 3.804% to 5.608% is only 1.804 percentage points wide, smaller than the declared resolution, so that sub-band should not be treated as a reliably distinct empirical category.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A rheological contrast could be overstated as evidence for a specific microscopic encounter-frequency mechanism that the planned measurement cannot identify.
objections.objection: No target-result leakage is evident. However, M-HOLD-120 measures only viscosity drift. A result below 3.804% can establish superlinear suppression relative to the registered numerical baseline, but it cannot establish H-RESIN's stated explanation that suppression occurs by lowering the effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species within a non-reactive continuum. The modifier's chemical inertness is also not measured.

skeptic.recommended_change: Replace the single-card experiment with a preregistered matched set that includes: an E2 reactive-core-only 120 C hold to establish the relevant baseline; S1C49 acrylic-only; and a matched nonzero-tackifier formulation for H-DUAL. Verify the acrylic and tackifier reactive-group contents and recalculate NCO:OH before assigning phi_r. Where possible, include an inert-dilution control at the same reactive mass fraction. Use at least three independent preparations per composition and preregister the replicate summary, uncertainty interval, and boundary rule before observing results.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 7.608% H-CORE benchmark is transferred from one unreplicated E1 hold despite S1C49 using the compositionally and stoichiometrically different E2 core, for which no hold baseline exists. This makes the central dilution-versus-superlinear comparison dependent on an untested cross-core transfer rather than a matched control.

design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
